    Reflecting an indecomposable representation at a sink #

    The Bernstein-Gelfand-Ponomarev reflection at a sink i replaces the vertex space Mᵢ by the kernel of the sum LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.incomingSum of the arrows into i, and it acts on dimension vectors by the simple reflection sᵢ whenever that sum is onto (LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.dimVector_reflectRep). This file discharges that hypothesis: the sum of the arrows into a sink is onto for every indecomposable representation except the vertex simple Sᵢ, which is the representation the reflection annihilates.

    One construction does the work. A linear endomorphism π of Mᵢ that the paths through i do not see extends by the identity at the other vertices to an endomorphism LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.vertexEnd of the whole representation, idempotent as soon as π is. The category of representations is abelian, hence idempotent complete, so an indecomposable object carries no idempotent endomorphism besides 0 and the identity (LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.idempotent_eq_zero_or_id_of_indecomposable), and therefore π itself is 0 or the identity. Applied to the projection onto the range of the incoming sum along a complement, this says the range is all of Mᵢ unless M vanishes away from i; applied to the projection onto a line, it says a representation concentrated at i is a line there, hence is Sᵢ, provided i carries no nontrivial closed path.

    LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.vertexEnd is stated at a vertex, not at a sink: naturality needs only that no path from elsewhere into i sees π before it, that no path from i to elsewhere sees π after it, and that π commutes with the maps of closed paths at i. At a sink the second condition is vacuous and all closed paths are trivial; the dual construction at a source, in LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.RepresentationTheory.Quiver.Reflection.Source.Indecomposable, is the same theorem with the first condition vacuous instead.

    Main definitions #

    • LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.vertexEnd: the endomorphism of M acting by a given endomorphism of Mᵢ at a vertex i and by the identity elsewhere, with LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.vertexEnd_eq_id_iff and LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.vertexEnd_eq_zero_iff recognizing when it is trivial.

    Main results #

    • LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.vertexIdempotent_eq_id_or_eq_zero_of_indecomposable: an idempotent of Mᵢ invisible to the paths through i is the identity, or is zero and M vanishes away from i, with LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.sinkIdempotent_eq_id_or_eq_zero_of_indecomposable its form at a sink, where the hypothesis reads "π fixes the image of every arrow into i".
    • LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.exists_ne_zero_span_eq_top_of_forall_subsingleton, LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.dimVector_eq_single_of_forall_subsingleton and LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.nonempty_iso_simpleRep_of_forall_subsingleton: an indecomposable representation concentrated at a vertex with no nontrivial closed path is a line there, hence isomorphic to the vertex simple.
    • LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.nonempty_iso_of_forall_subsingleton: two such representations concentrated at the same vertex are isomorphic; unlike the comparison with the vertex simple, this needs no restriction on universes.
    • LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.incomingSum_surjective_of_indecomposable: the sum of the arrows into a sink is onto for every indecomposable representation not isomorphic to the vertex simple there.
    • LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.dimVector_reflectRep_of_indecomposable: consequently the reflection at a sink acts on the dimension vector of such a representation by the simple reflection at that vertex.

    Implementation notes #

    LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.sinkIdempotent_eq_id_or_eq_zero_of_indecomposable takes its hypothesis on π in the form "π fixes the image of each arrow into i" rather than "π fixes the range of LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.incomingSum". The two agree on a finite quiver, by LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.map_toPath_mem_range_incomingSum, but the arrow form needs no finiteness, and neither then do the construction, its recognition lemmas, or the statement that an indecomposable representation concentrated at a sink is a line there. Finiteness enters only where LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.incomingSum does.

    The results comparing M with LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.simpleRep k Q i are stated in the last section, where the quiver, its arrows and the field all live in one universe. This is forced, not chosen: the vertex spaces of a reflected representation are cut out of a product indexed by the arrows, so LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.reflectRep needs them in max v w x, while Sᵢ puts the field itself at i and so needs them in the universe of the field. A statement mentioning both therefore has to identify the two, and the general statements above -- which name no vertex simple -- are proved in the wider setting and specialize to it.

    As in the neighbouring files, a vertex i : Q is used as an object of the free category CategoryTheory.Paths Q, which is Q only by unfolding a semireducible definition. Rewriting cannot see through that identification, so every step that branches on equality of vertices is factored through a lemma quantified over Q, and the components of LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.vertexEnd are supplied by the private vertexEndApp; LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.vertexEnd_app_self and LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.vertexEnd_app_of_ne are the interface.

    References #

    This is the identity dim (C⁺ᵢ M) = sᵢ · dim M with its hypothesis discharged. See Bernstein--Gelfand--Ponomarev, Coxeter functors and Gabriel's theorem, and Derksen--Weyman, An Introduction to Quiver Representations, Ch. 2.

    The endomorphism attached to an idempotent at a vertex #

    source
    noncomputable def LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.vertexEnd {k : Type u} {Q : Type v} [Field k] [Quiver Q] (M : QuiverRep k Q) {i : Q} (π : ↑(M.obj i) →ₗ[k] ↑(M.obj i)) (hin : ∀ (a : Q) (p : Quiver.Path a i), a ≠ i → ∀ (z : ↑(M.obj a)), π ((ModuleCat.Hom.hom (M.map p)) z) = (ModuleCat.Hom.hom (M.map p)) z) (hout : ∀ (b : Q) (p : Quiver.Path i b), b ≠ i → ∀ (y : ↑(M.obj i)), (ModuleCat.Hom.hom (M.map p)) (π y) = (ModuleCat.Hom.hom (M.map p)) y) (hcomm : ∀ (p : Quiver.Path i i), CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp (M.map p) (ModuleCat.ofHom π) = CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp (ModuleCat.ofHom π) (M.map p)) :
    M ⟶ M

    The endomorphism of M given by an endomorphism at one vertex. For a linear endomorphism π of Mᵢ that no path into i from elsewhere sees before it (hin), that no path out of i to elsewhere sees after it (hout), and that commutes with every closed-path map at i (hcomm), this is the endomorphism of M acting by π at i and by the identity at every other vertex.

    The three hypotheses hold at a sink and, dually, at a source; they are what naturality asks for, one case of the square for each of the four positions of i relative to the ends of a path.

      Two indecomposable representations concentrated at the same vertex are isomorphic, provided that vertex carries no closed path but the trivial one. Each is a line at that vertex and zero elsewhere, and no arrow joins the vertex to itself, so any linear isomorphism of the two lines is an isomorphism of representations.

      The surjectivity of the incoming sum #

      source
      theorem LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.incomingSum_surjective_or_forall_subsingleton {k : Type u} {Q : Type v} [Field k] [Quiver Q] {M : QuiverRep k Q} {i : Q} [Fintype Q] [(a b : Q) → Fintype (a ⟶ b)] (hi : Quiver.IsSink i) (hM : CategoryTheory.Indecomposable M) :
      Function.Surjective ⇑(incomingSum M i) ∨ ∀ (a : Q), a ≠ i → Subsingleton ↑(M.obj a)

      The sum of the arrows into a sink of an indecomposable representation is onto, unless the representation is concentrated at that sink. This is the surjectivity hypothesis of LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.dimVector_reflectRep, discharged: the range of the incoming sum is a direct summand of Mᵢ, so a proper range would split M, and the only splitting an indecomposable representation admits leaves nothing outside the sink.

      The vertex simple as the exceptional case #
